intended_object: The map on morphisms of the scalar-extension functor K ⊗_R – on topological R-modules: a continuous R-linear map g : M → N gives the continuous K-linear map id_K ⊗ g : K ⊗_R M → K ⊗_R N, sending c ⊗ m to c ⊗ g(m). This comes from the docstring, the module documentation and its later use as `map` in the functor.
explanation:
The underlying linear map is `mapLinear R K g`. Its function is `TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id g`, which the library proves K-linear for the left K-action on K ⊗_R M (k • (c ⊗ m) = (k*c) ⊗ m). Continuity comes from `mapRCLM`, the continuous tensor map on the R-view, which carries the same topology. The two topologies are compared by identity homeomorphisms, so the continuity proof is legitimate. The lemma `mapCLM_tmul` confirms that c ⊗ m goes to c ⊗ g m, which is exactly id ⊗ g. This is the standard functorial action of extension of scalars.

On generality: R is a commutative ring and K is any R-algebra, possibly noncommutative, with the discrete topology. Discreteness is what makes the K-action on the tensor topology jointly continuous, so the object depends on that hypothesis. The construction is not a restriction of something more general. Mathlib has only the algebraic version, `ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.map`, which also needs a commutative target ring. It has no topological-module version, so this definition is not too narrow.
